solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Even gang arriving in pieces

parts.note: even means level or flat
a gang is a pack, as in a pack of thieves

explanation.surface: A level-headed crew turns up in bits and pieces, like a group of friends straggling in.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-assembly furniture is sold boxed as separate parts, so it is delivered in pieces for the buyer to build.

clue.text: Figure out the downward distance

definitions.meaning: to figure out is to understand or work out
a nautical unit of six feet used for measuring the depth of water

explanation.surface: Calculate how far it is down to the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to comprehend; the noun is a sailor's measure of depth, six feet.

clue.text: Nanny reciting poem dedicated to fruit?

indicators.note: reciting means saying out loud, so the clue's phrase is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a poem addressed to a fruit would open 'O pear', in the style of an apostrophising ode

explanation.surface: A childminder declaims verses in praise of a fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'O pear', spoken, sounds like the French phrase for a live-in foreign helper.
explanation.definitionFit: A young foreign helper living with a family and minding the children is loosely a nanny.

clue.text: Riddle regarding pig's second pizza topping

parts.note: to riddle with holes is to pepper, as with shot
on means about or regarding

indicators.note: points to the second letter of the word pig

explanation.surface: A puzzle concerning which pizza topping a pig would choose.
explanation.definitionFit: A spicy sausage sliced thinly is a very common thing to scatter over a pizza.

clue.text: Walk authorised by the state

definitions.meaning: a short walk taken for one's health
permitted under the nation's founding law, i.e. lawful by the charter of government

explanation.surface: A stroll that has official government approval.
explanation.definitionFit: A health-giving stroll is a noun sense; the adjective means in keeping with the nation's founding legal document.

clue.text: Insect could prove annoying?

parts.note: may expresses possibility, like could
to bug someone is to irritate them

explanation.surface: A creepy-crawly might turn out to be a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockchafer, a large beetle out in late spring, is a familiar type of beetle insect.

clue.text: Initially, astonishingly befuddled brain offered therapy to get head in order

indicators.note: tells us to take the opening letter of each of the next five words

explanation.surface: A confused mind is surprisingly given treatment to tidy things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head in order' reads as 'sort things out' but is the definition: the head of a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: The superior of a monastery heads that community of monks, a religious order.

clue.text: Card game where a club has the measure of diamonds, after bad lead

indicators.note: the remaining pieces follow the opening one
the lead of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: C is the card abbreviation for clubs
gem weight is measured in carats

explanation.surface: A card game in which a club suit is valued in gem weights after a poor opening.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino gambling game played with cards, famously favoured by James Bond.

clue.text: One can't see you supporting girl breaking sergeant's heart

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece goes underneath
the girl's word breaks into the middle pair of letters
the heart of a word is its central letters, here two from the eight-letter sergeant

parts.note: lass is a girl
ye is old-fashioned you

explanation.surface: A girl comes between a sergeant and his affections, and you prop them up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supporting' places YE beneath GLASSE.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificial eye made of glass gives no vision, so it is something that cannot see.

clue.text: US biscuits with grain lacking in meat and nuts

indicators.note: lacking means without, so a word is dropped from grain

parts.note: the clue's own word in is the part removed
ham is a meat
crackers and nuts both mean mad

explanation.surface: American biscuits made from cereal without any meat or nuts in them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet wholemeal crackers are an American snack, used for s'mores; Americans call such things crackers rather than biscuits.

clue.text: Tennis player's skill, with shot gaining point on return

indicators.note: return means going back, so the whole combination is read backwards
the first piece acquires the second after it

parts.note: a nip is a small shot of spirits
a spot is a point or place

explanation.surface: A tennis player wins a point with a shot as the ball comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' and 'return' look like tennis but give a dram of whisky and a reversal: NIPSPOT read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward rotation put on a struck ball is a skill tennis players use to make it dip.

clue.text: Girl in novel starts to clown around on old instrument

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece on another means following it

parts.note: the rebec is a medieval bowed stringed instrument

indicators.note: the opening letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A girl from a book fools about on an antique instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Daphne du Maurier's 1938 novel is named after the hero's dead first wife, so she is a girl in a novel.

clue.text: In reserve, all nasty then?

parts.note: if not a single thing is pleasant, then everything is nasty: the phrase is a cryptic paraphrase of zero followed by a word for pleasant

explanation.surface: Holding something back, so everything turns unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: No clue word maps onto a piece alone: 'all nasty' as a whole is paraphrased as none pleasant, O plus NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans put on hold or kept for later are frozen, an idiom for being kept in reserve.

clue.text: Islanders a success in the conversion of saint

indicators.note: the pair goes inside the rearranged letters
converting changes form, so the letters of saint are rearranged

parts.note: a hit is a success

explanation.surface: Island folk are a hit in turning a saint, as missionaries would hope.
explanation.definitionFit: People of a Polynesian island in French Polynesia are islanders.

clue.text: Modern poem turned into the opposite

indicators.note: the reworked letters go inside the other word

parts.note: contrary means the opposite

indicators.note: turned means changed around, so poem's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An up-to-date poem became its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to the present day is a synonym for modern.

clue.text: Arrest boy playing up in seafood restaurant

indicators.note: misbehaving, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Police detain a misbehaving lad in a fish restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A counter or eatery serving shellfish is a kind of seafood restaurant.

clue.text: Lick man in depressed baldie

indicators.note: the two pieces sit within the word for depressed

parts.note: depressed means sad
to lap is to lick, as a cat does
he stands for a man

explanation.surface: Hit a man inside a gloomy bald fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: SLAPHEAD is British slang, mildly insulting, for a bald man.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang term for a man with no hair, the same as a baldie.

clue.text: Head of organisation in otherwise reviled criminal

indicators.note: that letter is placed inside the rearranged letters
otherwise means in another way, so reviled's letters are reordered
the head of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: The boss of a gang is inside, a despised crook.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer, someone who commits wicked acts, is a criminal.

clue.text: Romantic subplot nothing to be concerned about?

parts.note: love means zero in tennis scoring
an interest is a thing one is concerned with

explanation.surface: A side-plot about romance that is nothing to worry about.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface 'nothing to be concerned about' must be split: 'nothing' and 'to be concerned about'.
explanation.definitionFit: A character's sweetheart, and the romantic strand around them, is a standard subplot term.

clue.text: Pick up large animal, struggling to speak

indicators.note: to pick up is to hear, so the word is taken as heard

parts.note: a horse is a large animal

explanation.surface: Try lifting a big beast and you end up short of breath.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough croaky voice from a sore throat makes it hard to speak.

clue.text: Answer that's found in a laboratory

definitions.meaning: a glass vessel with a long bent neck used for distilling

explanation.surface: A reply that is discovered among lab equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a witty reply and a long-necked distilling flask used by chemists.

clue.text: Very old Australian arrested by police, a suspect

indicators.note: an arrested piece is held within the other
suspect here is an adjective meaning dodgy, so the letters are unreliable and rearranged

parts.note: Oz is the informal name for Australia

explanation.surface: An elderly Aussie is detained by officers as a suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: The geological era from about 540 to 250 million years ago is extremely ancient.

clue.text: Duck on trailer of sheep

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: a duck is a score of zero in cricket, shaped like O
a vine is a trailing plant

explanation.surface: A duck rides on a sheep's trailer.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relating to sheep, as bovine relates to cattle.

clue.text: Eat before pocketing half of food

indicators.note: pocketing means taking in, so the other piece goes inside

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before

indicators.note: the back half of the four-letter word food

explanation.surface: Have a meal before stashing away some of the food.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat away at something, like rust or water on rock, is to wear it down gradually.

clue.text: Beethoven's Fourth interrupting his Third? That's naughty!

indicators.note: the letter breaks into the other word

parts.note: Beethoven's Third Symphony is the Eroica

indicators.note: points to the fourth letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: A cheeky concert-goer's quip about Beethoven's symphonies running into each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beethoven's Fourth' looks like the symphony but is the letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexually explicit art or literature is risqué, the stuff someone might call naughty.

clue.text: Red light for commercial trade turning amber, then green

indicators.note: turning means changing, so amber's letters are rearranged

parts.note: a green light means go

explanation.surface: Traffic lights cycling from red through amber to green, applied to commerce.
explanation.definitionFit: An official ban on trade with a country stops commerce, as a stop signal halts traffic.

clue.text: Mended socks, remarkably

definitions.meaning: repaired holes in hosiery by weaving thread across them
a mild intensifier meaning very or extremely, as in a ___ good idea

explanation.surface: Fixed one's socks surprisingly well.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb is past tense of mending knitwear with needle and yarn; the euphemistic adverb means extremely.

clue.text: Tureen is demolished, as hungry

indicators.note: a demolished thing is broken up, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A soup bowl is smashed, as is a hungry diner's appetite.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal literary adjective meaning greedy or ravenous.
